purpose: Distinguish mathematically meaningful geometry/process/security structures from merely suggestive shapes before transferring them into Foundry, House, policy, proof or planning.
admission_rule: Name the invariant/constraint/objective first. Choose a shape or method only if its mathematics/process semantics implement that invariant. Reject visual analogy without operational consequence.

classes.meaning: Metric/affine/projective relations where coordinates, distances, incidence or centers have mathematical force.
Connectivity, crossing, adjacency and coloring constraints; geometry may deform while graph structure remains.
Tradeoffs among several objectives; simplex only when a conserved composition exists, Pareto when objectives can vary independently.
Divergence/convergence or staged work models; shape denotes workflow, not metric geometry.
Goal/threat/risk frameworks; labels are dimensions or categories, not points in a Euclidean figure unless explicitly modeled that way.

methods.name: Simplex / barycentric triangle
methods.law: Three non-negative weights normalized to sum to 1 identify a point in a 2-simplex.
methods.use_when: The state is genuinely a conserved three-way composition or allocation.
methods.do_not_use: Three objectives are independent, can all rise/fall together, or do not exhaust a fixed budget.
methods.current_transfer: Triangle Bench allocation gesture only; useful elsewhere only with an explicit sum constraint.

methods.name: Triangle centers / Euler line
methods.law: Different center definitions preserve different criteria; O, G, H and N lie on the Euler line, while I generally follows a different relation.
methods.use_when: The center criterion itself maps to a real invariant: balance, equal vertex distance, side clearance, etc.
methods.do_not_use: Assign semantic meaning after seeing an attractive construction.
methods.current_transfer: Center Lab explanatory probe; no canonical project prioritization mapping.

methods.name: Planarity / K₃,₃ utilities graph
methods.law: K₃,₃ is non-planar; Kuratowski characterizes non-planarity via subdivisions of K₃,₃ or K₅.
methods.use_when: Routing on one layer/surface must avoid crossings and the graph topology is the actual constraint.
methods.do_not_use: Crossovers, multiple layers, bridges, 3D routing or time-multiplexing are available and legal.
methods.current_transfer: Candidate diagnostic for House wiring/hoses/marks/routes: proves when a single planar layer is structurally insufficient.

methods.name: Graph coloring
methods.law: Assign labels/colors so adjacent conflicting graph elements receive different labels; the required number depends on the graph.
methods.use_when: Objects that conflict through adjacency/interference must be assigned channels, tools, times, markings or resources.
methods.do_not_use: The problem is routing/planarity. The utilities problem is not a three-color theorem.
methods.current_transfer: Candidate for channel/resource allocation, House marks, mutually incompatible operations or tool scheduling.

methods.name: Voronoi / Delaunay dual
methods.law: Voronoi partitions space by nearest site; Delaunay connects sites with adjacent Voronoi regions.
methods.use_when: Nearest-resource territory and neighborhood adjacency are real spatial questions.
methods.do_not_use: Semantic importance or workflow dependency is being mistaken for physical proximity.
methods.current_transfer: Strong candidate for House nearest-tool/resource lookup, sensor coverage and spatial adjacency.

methods.name: Pareto frontier
methods.law: Keep non-dominated alternatives: no other feasible option is at least as good in every objective and strictly better in one.
methods.use_when: Several independent objectives conflict and no single weighting is justified.
methods.do_not_use: A fixed budget already makes barycentric/simplex allocation the correct model, or one objective is a hard constraint rather than a tradeoff.
methods.current_transfer: High-value candidate for shopping/procurement, build choices, latency/privacy/cost tradeoffs and hardware selection.

methods.name: Design Council Double Diamond
methods.law: Discover and Develop diverge; Define and Deliver converge. The process explicitly allows returning to earlier stages as learning changes the problem.
methods.use_when: A design/research problem needs disciplined divergence before commitment and another divergence before delivery.
methods.do_not_use: A known bounded repair/action is already specified; adding discovery would only delay execution.
methods.current_transfer: Donor for RECOVER/INVESTIGATE → SPECIFY → IMPLEMENT/VERIFY rhythm; not a replacement for RETURN or current control.

methods.name: CIA security triad
methods.law: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability are distinct assurance objectives.
methods.use_when: Checking whether a system/security change protects information access, correctness and service availability.
methods.do_not_use: Treating CIA as a simplex whose components must sum to a fixed budget, or assuming a literal geometric triangle adds security meaning.
methods.current_transfer: Baseline checks for Human Port, Router/Policy, local agents, House control endpoints and public/private projections.

methods.name: STRIDE threat categories
methods.law: Classify threats as Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service or Elevation of Privilege.
methods.use_when: Threat-modeling an actual data flow, trust boundary, actor/resource or control endpoint.
methods.do_not_use: As a decorative checklist without assets, trust boundaries and mitigations.
methods.current_transfer: Very strong candidate for Router/Policy, HUMAN PORT delegation, contact surfaces and House automation authority.

methods.name: NIST Privacy Framework
methods.law: Manage privacy risk as an organizational/system risk problem rather than reducing privacy to secrecy alone.
methods.use_when: Personal data, health/care context, people, cameras/sensors or delegated agents create privacy risk over a lifecycle.
methods.do_not_use: As a geometry or as proof that a particular implementation is private.
methods.current_transfer: Baseline donor for private adapters, Human Port, House sensing and any future continuous personal-data ingestion.

bounded_tests.head: HOUSE / SPATIAL
bounded_tests.question: Can one real routing/marking problem be represented as a graph where a single-layer planar constraint changes the design decision?

bounded_tests.head: HOUSE / SPATIAL
bounded_tests.question: Does nearest-resource / adjacency projection improve one actual tool, sensor or zone decision over ordinary plan view?

bounded_tests.head: FIELD INDEX / procurement
bounded_tests.question: Does Pareto pruning remove dominated purchase/build options without inventing weights?

bounded_tests.head: HUMAN PORT / Router / Policy
bounded_tests.question: Can STRIDE reveal one missing trust-boundary control not already represented by current policy schemas?

bounded_tests.head: recovery → implementation
bounded_tests.question: Does explicit divergence/convergence reduce premature building on one ambiguous recovered branch, or does existing RECOVER→DISTINGUISH→ENACT→RETURN already dominate it?
